settings.label: Updates from the fields:
settings.heading: Our goal: bring life back to neglected pockets of Tuscan land.
settings.text: UNTO started as a rural recovery project in the hills of Florence. The land fed people for centuries, then emptied out from the 1950s. We work with small farms to keep it producing, starting with olive oil.
settings.alt_1: Harvesting olives with a pole rake over green nets in the Tuscan hills
settings.alt_2: Fresh green olive oil pouring out at the mill

settings.a:
Yes. Add a gift message in your cart and enter their address at checkout.

Sending to several people? Place one order per address.

settings.q: What do I do with it?
settings.a: Pour it on things. Warm bread, beans, soup, roast potatoes, a fried egg. Add it at the end, off the heat.
New-season Tuscan oil is green and grassy, with a peppery kick at the back of the throat. The pepper is a sign of fresh oil, and it softens over the months.
The best-before date is printed on the tin. Keep it somewhere cool and dark. It's at its best young, so don't save it for a special occasion.

settings.q: Where does the oil come from?
settings.a: From a small farm in the hills around Florence. UNTO started as a project to bring neglected Tuscan land back into use. Read the story.
Italian for new oil: the first oil of the season, pressed in autumn, at its greenest and most peppery. In Tuscany people wait all year for it.
